subject: zoology_2
question_text: Describe chromosomal theory of sex determination.

mark_split.label: Sex chromosomes and the two methods
How the grasshopper's sex is decided
How a human child's sex is decided

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book pp.21-22, LAQ 7. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 after the examiner audit: the opening line no longer says the sex pair is always X and Y, which the card's own ZO-ZZ and ZW-ZZ steps contradict, and the insider note now lists the four types instead of claiming a mark cap.

steps.label: The two methods
steps.why: Whichever sex makes two kinds of gamete is the one that decides the sex of the offspring, and that is what splits the methods in two.
common_mistakes: Calling sex chromosomes autosomes. They are allosomes.
steps.memory_tip: Heterogametic means making two kinds of gamete.
steps.margin_note: Name both methods, then take them in turn.
lines: In most animals a pair of chromosomes
decides the sex. They are called sex
chromosomes, or allosomes.
The sex chromosomes are called X and Y in
some animals, and Z and W in others.
There are two types of sex chromosomal
mechanism:
1. Male heterogametic method
2. Female heterogametic method

steps.label: XX-XO type
steps.why: The male has no partner for his single X, so half his sperm carry an X and half carry none.
common_mistakes: Giving the grasshopper male a Y chromosome. He has none.
Writing AAXX for the male. That is the female.
steps.memory_tip: XO means the male has one X and nothing opposite it.
lines: It is found in grasshoppers.
The karyotype of the female is AAXX and
of the male is AAXO.
Females have two X chromosomes and males
have only one.
The unpaired X chromosome decides the sex
of the offspring.

steps.label: The grasshopper cross
steps.why: All the ova are alike, so whichever kind of sperm arrives is what settles the sex.
common_mistakes: Making the ovum decide the sex here. The sperm does.
Forgetting that half the sperm carry no X at all.
steps.memory_tip: AX sperm gives a female, A sperm gives a male.
lines: The sperms are of two types: 50% carry AX
and 50% carry only A.
All the ova carry AX chromosomes.
The sex of the offspring is decided by the
sperm that fertilises the ovum.
If an AX sperm fertilises, the child is
female. If an AO sperm fertilises, the
child is male.

steps.label: XX-XY type
steps.why: Here the male's second sex chromosome is a Y rather than nothing, so his two kinds of sperm are X-carrying and Y-carrying.
common_mistakes: Calling the human female heterogametic. She is homogametic.
Writing AAXO for the human male.
steps.memory_tip: Female AAXX is homogametic; male AAXY is heterogametic.
steps.margin_note: Same pattern as XX-XO. Keep the layout identical.
lines: It is found in human beings.
The female is homogametic with karyotype
AAXX. The male is heterogametic with
karyotype AAXY.
Females have two X chromosomes. Males have
one X and one Y chromosome.
The Y chromosome decides the sex of the
offspring.

steps.label: The human cross
steps.why: Since every ovum carries an X, the child's sex depends entirely on whether the sperm brought an X or a Y.
common_mistakes: Blaming the mother for the child's sex. The sperm decides it.
Leaving out the karyotypes of the children.
steps.memory_tip: AX sperm gives a daughter, AY sperm gives a son.
steps.margin_note: Give the child's karyotype in brackets.
lines: 50% of the sperms are AX and the other 50%
are AY. All the ova contain AX.
The sex of the offspring is decided by the
sperm that fertilises the ovum.
If an AX sperm fertilises, the child is
female (AAXX).
If an AY sperm fertilises, the child is
male (AAXY).

steps.label: ZO-ZZ type
steps.why: In these animals it is the female that makes two kinds of gamete, so the letters are changed to Z and W to avoid confusion with X and Y.
common_mistakes: Using X and Y letters here. The female heterogametic types use Z and W.
Making the male heterogametic in this type.
steps.memory_tip: Z and W are used when the FEMALE is the heterogametic sex.
steps.margin_note: Name the animal for each type.
lines: It is found in Fumea moths.
The karyotype of the female is AAZO and of
the male is AAZZ.
The female is heterogametic with one Z
chromosome. The male is homogametic with
two Z chromosomes.
The sex of the offspring is decided by the
ovum that is fertilised.
If an AO ovum is fertilised it will be
female. If an AZ ovum is fertilised it will
be male.

steps.label: ZW-ZZ type
steps.why: The bird's female carries two different sex chromosomes, so the egg rather than the sperm settles the chick's sex.
common_mistakes: Making the male bird heterogametic. The female is.
lines: It is found in birds.
The karyotype of the female is AAZW and of
the male is AAZZ.
The female is heterogametic with Z and W
chromosomes. The male is homogametic with
ZZ chromosomes.
If an AZ ovum is fertilised it will be
male. If an AW ovum is fertilised it will
be female.

steps.label: Diagram — the human cross
steps.why: The crossing lines show at a glance that the ovum is always the same and only the sperm varies.
common_mistakes: Drawing two kinds of ovum. All ova carry AX.
Leaving the karyotypes off the children.
steps.memory_tip: One kind of ovum, two kinds of sperm, two kinds of child.
steps.margin_note: Draw the cross for the human XX-XY type.

insider_note: Four types, two under each method. The complete answer names all four with the animal each belongs to: XX-XO grasshopper, XX-XY human, ZO-ZZ Fumea moth, ZW-ZZ bird.
